summary: Expressway USA Freightlines is a family-owned, asset-based drayage and container freight station operator in Carteret, NJ, running import/export container moves between the NY/NJ piers and its CFS/warehouse, plus transloading, consolidation and cold/frozen storage. Founded in 1982 and still run by the Fleischer family (Steve Fleischer, Owner/President; Alexis Fleischer, Vice President), it serves large beneficial cargo owners and 3PLs such as UPS Supply Chain Solutions, Costco and Kuehne+Nagel. Operations are phone/email- and dispatcher-driven, with a posted 40-50 truck morning dispatch and terminal appointment booking on APM and Port Liberty Bayonne systems.

facts.fact: Started in 1982; family-owned asset-based transportation provider located in Carteret, New Jersey, that owns and controls a fleet of 53+ trucks and chassis.

Company has been 100% owned and managed by the Fleischer family since inception, with three generations involved and two currently active: Steve Fleischer (Owner/President) and his daughter Alexis Fleischer (Vice President).
Services described as trucking/drayage, warehousing (including cold and frozen product, transloading from container to dry van, consolidation) and a Container Freight Station & Distribution Center.
Named customers include UPS Supply Chain Solutions, Costco, Kuehne+Nagel, Kraft Foods, Ace Hardware, BJ's Wholesale Club and Vanguard Logistics, described as clients of over 38 years.
Posted hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 am-5:00 pm, Saturday by appointment, Sunday closed; the contact page shows a live opening-hours widget but no quote request or booking tool.

FMCSA SAFER snapshot (data as of 11/09/2026): USDOT 188718, status ACTIVE, authorized for-hire motor carrier of property, MC-152998, MCS-150 filed 06/17/2025, 38 power units, 32 drivers, 151,239 miles (2024), satisfactory safety rating.
FMCSA lists the company's physical and mailing address as 49 West Ferris Street, East Brunswick, NJ 08816, phone (732) 366-8052.

Current job posting for a Port Dispatcher: 5:30am-2:30pm shift dispatching a fleet of 40-50 trucks/drivers to the NY/NJ piers, booking appointments on APM and Port Liberty Bayonne appointment systems, planning weekly schedule around vessel arrivals, scheduling customer delivery appointments, answering emails and phone calls, and order entry; $55,000-$65,000/yr.
The dispatcher posting lists knowledge of Port Pro (TMS) as a plus and Excel/Google Docs as required tools, and stresses avoiding additional charges and delays.
Website runs on GoDaddy Website Builder, carries a 2020 copyright, and the public sitemap contains only three pages (home, about-us, contact-us) with last-modified dates of 2023-04-19.
Company advertises membership in the National Safety Council and affiliation with Bi-State Motor Carriers and the NY/NJ Foreign Freight Forwarders & Brokers Association.

operations_signals: Intake appears phone/email-driven: the site is three pages with no quote form, online booking, rate request or customer portal; the contact page presents hours and news rather than a structured request path (https://expresswayusa.com/contact-us).

Office hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 am-5:00 pm, Saturday by appointment, Sunday closed, while dispatch starts at 5:30 am - a posted-hours versus operating-hours mismatch that implies early-morning driver and pier issues are handled outside stated office coverage (https://expresswayusa.com/contact-us, https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

Core coordination work is manual and exception-heavy: dispatchers book terminal appointments on APM and Port Liberty Bayonne systems, build the weekly plan around vessel arrivals, schedule customer delivery appointments and do order entry by hand (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

Customers are large BCOs and 3PLs (UPS Supply Chain Solutions, Costco, Kuehne+Nagel, Kraft, Ace Hardware, BJ's, Vanguard Logistics), implying EDI/email order flow and SLA-driven appointment compliance rather than consumer self-service (https://expresswayusa.com/about-us).

Two physical sites in play: Carteret terminal/CFS operations per company description, with the FMCSA-registered office address at 49 West Ferris Street, East Brunswick (https://expresswayusa.com/about-us, https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/query.asp?query_type=queryCarrierSnapshot&query_param=USDOT&query_string=188718).

Safety and compliance posture is formalized via National Safety Council membership and carrier-association affiliations, suggesting DOT/roadside-inspection recordkeeping is an ongoing administrative load (https://expresswayusa.com/contact-us).
hiring_signals: Actively hiring a Port Dispatcher for the 5:30am-2:30pm morning shift to run 40-50 trucks to the NY/NJ piers - a role whose listed duties are almost entirely repetitive coordination: appointment booking, schedule planning, customer delivery scheduling, email/phone handling and order entry (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

Posting asks for 1 year dispatching experience, 2 years customer service preferred, bilingual English/Spanish a plus, and ability to 'work without supervision' - indicating a lean office team where each dispatcher covers a wide span of duties (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

Benefits offered (401k, health/dental/vision, PTO, fuel reimbursement) suggest a stable, conventional small-carrier employment package rather than a gig-driver model (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

Indeed hosts a company profile with a Dispatcher job-title page and reported New Jersey dispatcher pay around $58.5k from 4 data points, indicating repeated dispatcher hiring over time (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Expressway-USA/job-titles/Dispatcher, https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Expressway-USA-1/salaries/Dispatcher/New-Jersey).
No careers section exists on the company website (only three pages in the sitemap), so hiring runs through third-party job boards rather than the site (https://expresswayusa.com/sitemap.website.xml).
review_themes: No customer-facing review content could be read: Yelp, Trustpilot, Indeed and Glassdoor returned blocks/CAPTCHAs, and no BBB profile surfaced in search results - so no verified themes on punctuality, billing or communication (https://www.yelp.com/biz/expressway-usa-freightlines-carteret).

An Indeed employer page exists with a small number of employee reviews (search result titled 'Working at EXPRESSWAY USA: 4 Reviews'), but the page body was not retrievable, so employer sentiment is unverified (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Expressway-USA/reviews).
tech_footprint: Marketing site is a GoDaddy Website Builder site with a 2020 copyright, a stale news/events block referencing 2020 activities, and a three-page sitemap last modified in April 2023 (https://expresswayusa.com/sitemap.website.xml, https://expresswayusa.com/contact-us).

No online booking, quote request, shipment tracking, customer login or e-commerce functionality is present on the public site; the only interactive element is a GoDaddy store-hours widget (https://expresswayusa.com/contact-us).

Dispatch stack implied by hiring: APM Terminals and Port Liberty Bayonne appointment systems for pier slots, plus Excel and Google Docs for planning (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

Port Pro (drayage TMS) familiarity is listed as a plus rather than a requirement, so it is unclear whether Port Pro is the incumbent system (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

Social/recruiting footprint is thin: a LinkedIn company page exists with roughly 80 followers describing the firm as an asset-based family-run drayage trucking company (https://www.linkedin.com/company/expressway-usa-freightlines-inc).
growth_signals: Company brands itself 'Since 1982 and still growing strong' and states its growth is fueled by world demand for international trade, with customers that have used its services for over 38 years (https://expresswayusa.com/about-us).

Hiring a second-shift-coverage-style morning dispatcher for a 40-50 truck fleet points to volume growth in pier drayage rather than contraction (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Ro1x_D-aKhga04w20KTIySLm4IcTvAEAairM7nHz8x9igplYyOeV4Q).

FMCSA MCS-150 filed in June 2025 and 151,239 miles reported for 2024 show a currently active, recently updated operating authority rather than a dormant carrier (https://safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/query.asp?query_type=queryCarrierSnapshot&query_param=USDOT&query_string=188718).

Service mix already spans drayage, CFS, transloading, consolidation and cold/frozen storage, a broader offering than pure trucking that supports cross-sell as import volumes shift (https://expresswayusa.com/).
decision_maker: Steve Fleischer, Owner/President (with Alexis Fleischer, Vice President) — listed on the company's own About Us page: https://expresswayusa.com/about-us

inferences.inference: Actual fleet and staff size is materially smaller than the website's '53+ trucks' headline, at roughly the mid-30s in power units and low-30s in drivers.
inferences.reasoning: FMCSA's MCS-150 filed 06/17/2025 lists 38 power units and 32 drivers; the website figure likely counts chassis and other equipment alongside tractors.

inferences.inference: The dispatch desk is the operational bottleneck and the highest-value place for an AI agent.
inferences.reasoning: One dispatcher posting covers 40-50 drivers plus terminal appointment booking on two port systems, vessel-arrival-driven weekly planning, customer delivery scheduling, order entry and inbound phone/email, while the posting explicitly warns against 'additional charges and or delays' - i.e., per-diem/demurrage exposure from missed appointment windows.

inferences.inference: A meaningful share of customer and driver inquiries arrive outside staffed hours and are likely missed.
inferences.reasoning: Dispatch starts at 5:30 am and drivers work the piers early, but posted office hours are 8:00 am-5:00 pm with Saturday by appointment only and no after-hours channel, chatbot or self-service tracking on the site.

inferences.inference: Quoting and order intake are handled manually per request rather than through a portal.
inferences.reasoning: The public site has no quote, booking, tracking or login functionality across its three pages, and the dispatcher job lists order entry as an essential function.

inferences.inference: Customer-service promises rest heavily on two family executives personally returning calls and emails.
inferences.reasoning: The About Us page states the President and Vice President 'return your email or call personally' and resolve issues themselves, which is a scaling constraint as volumes grow.

inferences.inference: Marketing and digital maturity is low, so outreach credibility is likely to come from operational ROI rather than existing tech adoption.
inferences.reasoning: GoDaddy template site with 2020 copyright, 2023 last update, three pages, ~80 LinkedIn followers, and job ads posted on third-party boards with no careers page.

data_gaps: No readable customer reviews: Yelp returned 403/CAPTCHA, Trustpilot 403, Google Maps is JS-only, and no BBB profile surfaced; customer satisfaction, on-time performance and billing-dispute themes cannot be characterized.
Indeed (company profile, reviews, dispatcher job titles) and Glassdoor were blocked to automated fetch; the 4-review count and $58.5k dispatcher pay figure come from search-result snippets only.
No revenue, employee headcount, warehouse square footage or container volume figures published anywhere accessible.
LinkedIn company page (follower count, headcount range, recent posts) could not be opened - 403.
Whether Port Pro TMS, EDI connections or a customer portal are actually in production is unknown; the job ad treats Port Pro as optional knowledge.

Third-party directory listings (MapQuest, YellowPages, whereorg) surface a Carteret street address at 1000 Port Carteret Drive and one listing claims a 100-truck fleet, but all of those pages were blocked or JS-only, so the address, terminal size and fleet figures are unverified.

No local news coverage of expansions, awards or new locations was found in the searches that succeeded; search providers were heavily rate-limited during this session, so absence of news is not proof of none.
